clue.text: One egg standing up in line, which is amazing

parts.note: a line of cord or thread is a string
one as the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word standing up is read from the bottom, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A single egg stands upright in a row of eggs, a remarkable sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the egg is turned over, not the 'one' before it; 'which is' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something staggering is so astonishing it almost makes you reel, a common synonym.

clue.text: In appearance too small to be unassailable

parts.note: an air is a look or manner
clothes too small for you are tight

explanation.surface: Something looks too slight to be beyond attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An airtight argument or case has no gaps, so it cannot be successfully attacked or challenged.

clue.text: Jan, a good man with a large jug

explanation.surface: Jan is a decent fellow carrying a big jug.
explanation.walkthrough: Jan Stewer is one of the riders in the English folk song Widecombe Fair, alongside Bill Brewer and Uncle Tom Cobley.
explanation.definitionFit: Jan Stewer is a named companion in the old Devon folk song, so his first name points to his surname.

clue.text: Second half of delivery is identical

explanation.definitionFit: In phrases like 'the very same man', the word means precisely that one, exactly identical.

clue.text: Fruit: shout about her choice

taken as written
a plum job or role is the choicest one

explanation.definitionFit: The cherry plum is a small round fruit of a wild plum tree, so it is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Irritates spaniel's head, which is uncalled for

clue.text: The end of the month, perhaps, so spread it thither

explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals the definition is only an example: not every month ends on its thirtieth day.

clue.text: Antelope from an eastern country

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern

clue.text: Understand a scheme to escape

taken as written

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Aunt Ryder switched to a cheaper fare

indicators.note: things switched around have changed places, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An aunt changes her travel plans to save money on a ticket.

explanation.definitionFit: British railways sell same-day round-trip tickets more cheaply than an ordinary return, so it is a reduced fare.

clue.text: Throw cold water on the record associated with our generation

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
taken as written
an age is a generation or era

clue.text: Informer facing informer, directly opposite

to as in face to face
the same slang again

explanation.surface: Two police informants confront one another.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people positioned face to face, very close and confronting each other, are in this idiomatic position.

clue.text: People can vary; it requires a mixture of sweets

if a job takes skill, it requires it

explanation.walkthrough: Liquorice Allsorts are a well-known British mixed liquorice sweet; the definition is the proverb's meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying is used to shrug at someone's odd behaviour, meaning human beings differ greatly in their tastes.

clue.text: Benevolence makes family end up with the saints

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Read about little Elizabeth being brought in

parts.note: taken as written

room as in scope or chance, room for improvement

clue.text: English sweetheart once turned up covering crown

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street

clue.text: One interrupting celebrities on the way up

the Roman numeral for one

clue.text: Deliver to Second Avenue

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

clue.text: Crush the newspapers

clue.text: Jane Eyre, perhaps, to go to Sunday school carrying Jules

parts.note: taken as written
Jules Verne, the French novelist
